techniques.name: Grid of failing tasks as a wordless problem hook
techniques.description: Six dark cards in a 3x2 grid (about 90% of the frame) appear within 9 frames, then a cursor visits them one by one; each card fills with draft lines and gets a small red or amber warning chip, roughly every half second, under a slow push-in of about 14%. In the last 5 frames every card is outlined in red or amber, then a hard cut to a light title card. The pain is a picture, so the later claim reads as relief.
techniques.routeReason: Flat 2D interface plus cursor and camera. If the cards show a real product's composer, it must be captured (capture:app) or rebuilt pixel-faithfully from a dated screenshot and played with ScreenPlayback under RegionCamera; a generic dashboard block may not stand in. Chips and outlines are simple timed overlays on top.

ease.name: power1.out
evidence: motion.json s001 camera push_in z 0.133, span90 3.38 s, gsap power1.out (pick was bezier; the bezier is a near-linear slow push)

techniques.name: Hard cut to an empty light frame, then a centred serif line fades in by word groups in place
techniques.description: The cut lands on one empty cream frame; on the next the first word group is at about 30% opacity and full by the third (3-frame fade, no movement, no blur). The line is laid out at its final centred width from the start, so later word groups (6 frames later in the first instance) fade in at their final positions and nothing reflows. A slow push-in of 4-6% runs under the whole card.
techniques.routeReason: Pure type on a flat ground; the reveal needs a layout measured once for the finished line with per-token opacity, which the sentence builder does not do yet.

techniques.name: Corner chat bubbles: request types top right, reply streams bottom left
techniques.description: While the centred title holds, a dark rounded bubble lands top right (fade from grey to near-black over 3 frames, F134-F136) and the user's request types into it at roughly two words a second. About 3.6 s later the reply bubble appears bottom left, rising and darkening over 5 frames (F242-F246), and its text streams a word every 2 frames (F246-F256). The slow human typing against the fast machine streaming is the contrast that sells the assistant.
techniques.routeReason: Generic chat bubbles over a title card are built from the chat block and typing schedule. If they show a specific assistant's chat interface, that interface must be captured or rebuilt pixel-faithfully from a dated screenshot.

evidence: speech-text.json request words at 4.517-7.517 s (2 fps sampling)

typography.entry: request types about two words a second; reply streams a word every 2 frames

techniques.name: One-bar dark loader with a self-drawing mark between ask and result
techniques.description: Hard cut to charcoal for exactly 4 beats. Frame 1: a dot. Frame 2: an orange disc. Frames 3-6: a white stroke loops through it and a violet disc grows beside it, forming a joined mark about 18% of frame width; a status label builds under it word by word; the stroke keeps travelling until the cut. A small attribution chip sits bottom left. Reused unchanged except the label.
techniques.routeReason: Two discs and one SVG stroke drawn along a path on a flat ground; the mark itself belongs to the brand and must be replaced by the new film's own mark or a neutral shape.

techniques.name: One source card bursts into a staggered grid of tailored cards
techniques.description: Caption fades (3 frames), the source card dissolves, and new cards spring out of its position one after another about 4 frames apart, each growing from about a third of its size to its cell of a 3x2 grid (about 85% of frame width), while a named cursor flag moves between them. Each card has a different layout for its destination.
techniques.routeReason: 2D layout animation of card rectangles from one origin to grid cells. The card contents are product interface, so they must be captured or faithfully rebuilt for the new product.

techniques.name: Dark toast rises under the finished grid
techniques.description: After the last check chip lands, a dark pill toast rises into the bottom centre (y about 0.86-0.90, 27% of width) over 5 frames and holds to the cut, stating the count and time of what was done.
techniques.routeReason: A single notification card; the toast block covers it with a one-item list.

techniques.name: Board fills under a slow drift, then the camera pulls back to the whole result
techniques.description: Empty grid, board fades in over 2 frames, then a cursor flag places events every 4-6 frames while the view drifts right about 16% of a frame width and in about 4% at constant speed for 2.4 s. At 24.93 s a pull-back of about 1.2x to 1.0x, fastest in its first 3 frames and settling over 15, reveals the whole board inside a rounded panel with a cream margin.
techniques.routeReason: One flat capture or replica of the board under RegionCamera keys: a linear drift, then an expo.out pull-back. The board is a product screen, so it must be captured (capture:app) at least 1.5x resolution or rebuilt pixel-faithfully.

techniques.name: Centred chat: request rises in, reply enters below and pushes it up
techniques.description: On near-black, the user bubble rises into the centre and settles in about 7 frames; 1.8 s later the reply bubble enters below and the pair shifts up together over about 6 frames, then small status chips appear inside the reply. No loader: the answer is immediate.
techniques.routeReason: The chat thread block does exactly this push-up. If it depicts a specific assistant's interface, capture it or rebuild it pixel-faithfully from a dated screenshot.

techniques.name: Live edit of the key word in a held line: select, delete, retype, recentre
techniques.description: A centred serif line holds; its first word sits in a pale blue selection with a named caret flag above it for about half a second. On the beat the selection is deleted and the replacement types at a letter a frame (7-8 frames for 7-8 letters) while the whole line recentres every frame. Swaps are 55 frames apart.
techniques.routeReason: Pure type: the rotating-word block already recentres a sentence around a changing slot; it needs a selection-and-retype mode instead of its roll.

techniques.name: Empty frame, mark pops with overshoot, tagline, fade to black
techniques.description: The claim line clears to one empty cream frame; the mark and wordmark fade and scale up from about 85% with roughly 8% overshoot, settling by about 12 frames; a one-line tagline with the address sits below. From 39.5 s the frame fades to black over 13 frames and holds black for the last 3.

techniques.name: Hard cuts every 4, 8 or 12 beats, two frames ahead of the hit, alternating light and dark grounds
techniques.description: No transition effects at all: nine hard cuts, each after 55, 111 or 166 frames (4, 8 or 12 beats at 129.3 BPM), placed 2-3 frames before the loudness peak of a hit. Most cuts also swap the ground between dark (L 4-11) and cream (L 87-95), which does the work a transition would do.
techniques.routeReason: Shot lengths from a beat grid of the new track and cuts snapped one or two frames early; existing sync helpers do both.

evidence: shots.json cut times; judged shot lengths 5.533, 1.834, 5.533, 3.700, 1.867, 5.533, 3.700, 5.533 s

sound.note: 8 of 9 cuts sit 0.07-0.10 s before a 50 ms loudness swell peak (a window of about 0.03 s out of a 0.46 s pulse, so roughly a 7% chance per cut; window chosen after looking), and from 9.233 s every cut is 0.03-0.07 s before a detected onset. sync.json's beat ratio (0.10 against 0.328 chance) is distorted by a tracker phase slip of about 0.2 s between 5.6 and 8.1 s. That the hits are a music kick is inferred; the track was not heard.
